newsitem.title: USA: Bond dealers oppose MSRB's draft OS delivery rule.
newsitem.headline: Bond dealers oppose MSRB's draft OS delivery rule.

text.p: The Bond Market Trade Association said it opposes MSRB's plan to tighten the deadline by which bond dealers must get final official statements to customers in primary municipal offerings.

The group, formerly called Public Securities Association, said in a comment letter to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board that the board has shown no evidence that customers are troubled by the present OS-delivery schedule.
The draft amendments would move up the time that a customer is to receive a final OS under the board's OS-delivery rule G-32.
The date would move from settlement to the day when final money confirmations are sent by dealers to customers.
The board proposed the revisions in mid-September and comments were due November 15.

BMTA said no-one has complained to the group that they are getting late deliveries of OSs. And, since the Securities and Exchange Commission published muni disclosure amendments in November 1994, more official statements are being produced and are reaching investers quicker, said BMTA's letter, signed by group Vice President George Brakatselos.
Brakatselos warned that the proposed amendments would "require many municipal securities dealers to make substantial changes to confirmation and official statement delivery systems."
"For example, dealers with branch offices have systems that generate and forward confirmations on trade date from the branch office making the sales," the group said.
"The proposed amendments would force dealers to incur enormous costs in changing such systems," the group said.

BMTA said rule G-32 already places great burdens on issuers and underwriters. "In some instances it is possible that the OS ... cannot be provided to a dealer in sufficient time to accompany final money confirmations," BMTA said.
